She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
Pea toe lea ai ʻa Sisu kiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Ko au ko e maama ʻo māmani: ko ia ʻoku muimui ʻiate au, ʻe ʻikai ʻalu ia ʻi he poʻuli, ka ʻe ʻiate ia ʻae maama ʻoe moʻui.”
Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
Ko ia naʻe pehē ai ʻae kau Fālesi kiate ia, “ʻOku ke fakamoʻoni kiate koe; ʻoku ʻikai moʻoni hoʻo fakamoʻoni.
The Pharisees therefore said unto him, Thou bearest record of thyself; thy record is not true.

Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ou fakamoʻoni kiate au, ka ʻoku moʻoni ʻeku fakamoʻoni: he ʻoku ou ʻilo ʻaia ʻoku ou haʻu mei ai, mo ia ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai; ka ʻoku ʻikai te mou ʻilo ʻaia ʻoku ou haʻu mei ai, pe ko ia ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai.
Jesus answered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye cannot tell whence I come, and whither I go.
‌ʻOku mou fakamaau fakakakano pē; ʻoku ʻikai te u fakamaau ha tokotaha.
Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no man.
Pea kapau te u fakamaau, ʻoku moʻoni ʻeku fakamaau he ʻoku ʻikai teu tokotaha pe, ka ko au mo e Tamai naʻa ne fekau au.
And yet if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.
Pea kuo tohi foki ʻi hoʻomou fono, ko e fakamoʻoni ʻae tangata ʻe toko ua ʻoku moʻoni.
It is also written in your law, that the testimony of two men is true.
Ko e tokotaha au ʻoku ou fakamoʻoni au, pea ko e Tamai naʻa ne fekau au ʻoku ne fakamoʻoni kiate au.”
I am one that bear witness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.
Pea naʻa nau pehē kiate ia, “Ko e fē hoʻo Tamai? Pea talaange ʻe Sisu, ʻOku ʻikai te mou ʻilo au, pe ko ʻeku Tamai: ka ne mou ʻilo au, pehē, kuo mou ʻilo mo ʻeku Tamai foki.
Then said they unto him, Where is thy Father? Jesus answered, Ye neither know me, nor my Father: if ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also.
Naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe Sisu ʻae ngaahi lea ni ʻi he tukunga koloa, ʻi heʻene akonaki ʻi he falelotu lahi: pea naʻe ʻikai puke ia ʻe ha taha; he naʻe teʻeki hokosia hono ʻaho.
These words spake Jesus in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no man laid hands on him; for his hour was not yet come.
Pea toe tala ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ou ʻalu, pea te mou kumi kiate au, ka te mou mate ʻi hoʻomou angahala: ko e potu ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai, ʻe ʻikai te mou hokosia.”
Then said Jesus again unto them, I go my way, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sins: whither I go, ye cannot come.
Pea pehē ai ʻae kakai Siu, “ʻE tāmateʻi ʻe ia ia? He ʻoku ne pehē, ‘Ko e potu ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai, ʻe ʻikai te mou hokosia.’”
Then said the Jews, Will he kill himself? because he saith, Whither I go, ye cannot come.
Pea tala ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku mei lalo ʻakimoutolu; ʻoku mei ʻolunga au: ʻoku ʻo māmani ʻakimoutolu; ʻoku ʻikai ʻo māmani au.
And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.
Ko ia naʻaku lea ai kiate kimoutolu, te mou mate ʻi hoʻomou angahala: he kapau ʻoku ʻikai te mou tui ‘ko au ia,’ te mou mate pe ʻi hoʻomou angahala.”
I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins.
Pea naʻa nau lea ai kiate ia, “Ko hai koe?” Pea pehēange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “ʻAia pe naʻaku tala ʻi muʻa kiate kimoutolu.”
Then said they unto him, Who art thou? And Jesus saith unto them, Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning.
‌ʻOku lahi ʻae meʻa ke u tala mo valokiʻi ʻiate kimoutolu: ka ko ia naʻa ne fekau au ʻoku moʻoni ia; pea ʻoku ou fakahā ki māmani ʻae ngaahi meʻa ko ia kuo u fanongo ʻiate ia.
I have many things to say and to judge of you: but he that sent me is true; and I speak to the world those things which I have heard of him.
Naʻe ʻikai te nau ʻilo ko ʻene lea kiate kinautolu ki he Tamai.
They understood not that he spake to them of the Father.

Pea pehē ai ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Hili hoʻomou hiki ki ʻolunga ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata, pea te mou toki ʻilo ‘ko au ia,’ pea mo ʻeku taʻefai-ha-meʻa ʻiate au pe; kae hangē hono akoʻi au ʻe heʻeku Tamai, ʻoku pehē ʻeku lea ki he ngaahi meʻa ni.
Then said Jesus unto them, When ye have lifted up the Son of man, then shall ye know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself; but as my Father hath taught me, I speak these things.
Pea ko ia naʻa ne fekau au ʻoku ʻiate au: ʻoku ʻikai siʻaki au ke tokotaha pe ʻe he Tamai; he ʻoku ou fai maʻuaipē ʻae ngaahi meʻa ʻoku lelei ai ia.”
And he that sent me is with me: the Father hath not left me alone; for I do always those things that please him.
Pea ʻi heʻene leaʻaki ʻae ngaahi lea ni, naʻe tui ʻae tokolahi kiate ia.
As he spake these words, many believed on him.
Pea pehē ai ʻe Sisu ki he kau Siu naʻe tui kiate ia, “Kapau te mou nofomaʻu ʻi heʻeku lea, pea ko ʻeku kau ākonga moʻoni ʻakimoutolu;
Then said Jesus to those Jews which believed on him, If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed;
Pea te mou ʻilo ʻae moʻoni, pea ʻe fakatauʻatāinaʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻe he moʻoni.”
And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.
Pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi kiate ia, “Ko e hako ʻo ʻEpalahame ʻakimautolu, pea naʻe ʻikai te mau pōpula ki ha taha: pea ʻoku fēfeeʻi ʻa hoʻo lau, ‘ʻE fakatauʻatāinaʻi ʻakimoutolu?’”
They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Ko ia ʻoku fai angahala, ko e pōpula ia ki he angahala.
Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.
Pea ʻoku ʻikai nofomaʻuaipē ʻi he fale ʻae pōpula: ka ʻoku nofomaʻuaipē ʻae ʻAlo.
And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever.
Ko ia kapau ʻe fakatauʻatāinaʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻe he ʻAlo, te mou tauʻatāina moʻoni.
If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
‌ʻOku ou ʻilo ko e hako ʻo ʻEpalahame ʻakimoutolu; ka ʻoku mou kumi ke tāmateʻi au, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ʻi homou loto ʻa ʻeku akonaki.
I know that ye are Abraham’s seed; but ye seek to kill me, because my word hath no place in you.
‌ʻOku ou lea ʻaki ʻaia kuo u ʻiloʻi ʻi heʻeku Tamai: pea ʻoku mou fai ʻaia kuo mou ʻiloʻi ʻi hoʻomou tamai.”
I speak that which I have seen with my Father: and ye do that which ye have seen with your father.
Naʻa nau leaange, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Ko ʻemau tamai ʻa ʻEpalahame.” Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Ka ne ko e fānau ʻa ʻEpalahame ʻakimoutolu, pehē, te mou fai ʻae ngaahi ngāue ʻa ʻEpalahame.
They answered and said unto him, Abraham is our father. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham.
Ka ko eni ʻoku mou kumi ke tāmateʻi au, ko e tangata kuo tala ʻae moʻoni kiate kimoutolu, ʻaia kuo u fanongo ʻi he ʻOtua: naʻe ʻikai fai pehē ʻe ʻEpalahame.
But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth, which I have heard of God: this did not Abraham.
‌ʻOku mou fai ʻae ngāue ʻa hoʻomou tamai.” Pea naʻa nau pehē ai kiate ia, “ʻOku ʻikai te mau tupu ʻi he feʻauaki; ʻoku taha pe ʻemau Tamai, ko e ʻOtua.”
Ye do the deeds of your father. Then said they to him, We be not born of fornication; we have one Father, even God.
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Ka ne ko hoʻomou Tamai ʻae ʻOtua, te mou ʻofa kiate au: he naʻaku tupu ai ʻo haʻu mei he ʻOtua; pea naʻe ʻikai te u haʻu ʻiate au pe, ka naʻa ne fekau au.
Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I proceeded forth and came from God; neither came I of myself, but he sent me.
Ko e hā ʻoku ʻikai ai te mou ʻilo ʻeku lea? Ka koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai te mou fie fai ki heʻeku akonaki.
Why do ye not understand my speech? even because ye cannot hear my word.

‌ʻOku mou ʻi hoʻomou tamai ko e tēvolo, pea ko e holi ʻa hoʻomou tamai te mou fai. Ko e fakapō ia talu mei he kamataʻanga, pea naʻe ʻikai nofomaʻu ʻi he moʻoni koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ha moʻoni ʻiate ia. ʻOka lea ʻaki ʻe ia ʻae loi, ʻoku ne lea ʻaki ʻene meʻa ʻaʻana: he ko e loi ia, mo e tamai ʻo ia.

Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.
Pea ko e meʻa ʻi heʻeku tala ʻae moʻoni kiate kimoutolu, ʻoku ʻikai ai te mou tui kiate au.
And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not.
Ko hai ʻiate kimoutolu ʻoku ne fakaʻilo haʻaku angahala? Pea kapau ʻoku ou lea ʻaki ʻae moʻoni ko e hā ʻoku ʻikai ai te mou tui kiate au?
Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me?
Ko ia ʻoku ʻi he ʻOtua, ʻoku fanongo ia ki he ngaahi folofola ʻae ʻOtua: pea pehē, ʻoku ʻikai te mou fanongo, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ʻi he ʻOtua ʻakimoutolu.”
He that is of God heareth God’s words: ye therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God.
Pea leaange ʻae kakai Siu, ʻonau pehē kiate ia, “ʻIkai ʻoku moʻoni ʻemau pehē, Ko e Samēlia koe, pea ʻoku ʻiate koe ha tēvolo?”
Then answered the Jews, and said unto him, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a devil?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu, “ʻOku ʻikai ha tēvolo ʻiate au; ka ʻoku ou fakaʻapaʻapa ki heʻeku Tamai, pea ʻoku mou fakalieliaʻi au.
Jesus answered, I have not a devil; but I honour my Father, and ye do dishonour me.
Pea ʻoku ʻikai teu kumi ʻae ongoongolelei ʻo ʻoku: ʻoku ai ha tokotaha ʻoku ne kumiʻi mo fakamaauʻi.
And I seek not mine own glory: there is one that seeketh and judgeth.
Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, Kapau ʻe fai ʻe ha tangata ki heʻeku lea, ʻe ʻikai ʻaupito mamata ia ki he mate.”
Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.

Pea lea ai ʻae kakai Siu kiate ia, “Ta ʻoku mau ʻilo ʻeni ʻoku ʻiate koe ha tēvolo. Kuo mate ʻa ʻEpalahame, mo e kau palōfita; ka ʻoku ke pehē, Kapau ʻe fai ʻe ha tangata ki heʻeku lea, ʻe ʻikai ʻaupito te ne kamata ʻae mate.
Then said the Jews unto him, Now we know that thou hast a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my saying, he shall never taste of death.
‌ʻOku ke lahi koe ki heʻemau tamai ko ʻEpalahame, ʻaia kuo mate? Pea, mate mo e kau palōfita: ʻoku ke pehē ko hai koe?”
Art thou greater than our father Abraham, which is dead? and the prophets are dead: whom makest thou thyself?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu, “Kapau te u fakaongolelei au, ko e meʻa noa pē ʻeku fakaongo: ko ʻeku Tamai ko ia ia ʻoku ne fakaongoleleiʻi au; ʻaia ʻoku mou pehē ai, ko homou ʻOtua ia:
Jesus answered, If I honour myself, my honour is nothing: it is my Father that honoureth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God:
Ka kuo ʻikai te mou ʻilo ia, ka ʻoku ou ʻilo ia: pea kapau te u pehē, ʻOku ʻikai te u ʻiloa ia, te u loi au ʻo hangē ko kimoutolu: ka ʻoku ou ʻilo ia, pe au tuitala ki heʻene folofola.
Yet ye have not known him; but I know him: and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be a liar like unto you: but I know him, and keep his saying.
Naʻe mātuʻaki fiefia ʻa hoʻomou tamai ko ʻEpalahame ke mamata ki hoku ʻaho: pea naʻe mamata ia, pea fiefia.
Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.
Pea lea ʻae kakai Siu kiate ia, “ʻOku teʻeki ai nimangofulu taʻu ho motuʻa, pea kuo ke mamata kia ʻEpalahame?”
Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, Ki muʻa ʻia ʻEpalahame, ‘ʻOku ou ʻi ai au.’”
Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.
Pea naʻa nau toʻo hake ʻae ngaahi maka, ke nau lisingi ʻaki ia; ka naʻe fufū ʻe Sisu ia, pea ʻalu ia ʻi honau lotolotonga mei he falelotu lahi, pea hao ai.
Then took they up stones to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.
Pea ʻi he ʻalu ange ʻa Sisu, ne mamata ia ki ha tangata naʻe fanauʻi ko e kui.
And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
Pea fehuʻi ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Lāpai, ko hai naʻe fai angahala, ʻae tangata ni, pe ko ʻene mātuʻa, naʻe fanauʻi kui ai ia?”
And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu, “Naʻe ʻikai fai angahala ʻae tangata ni, pe ko ʻene mātuʻa: ka ko e meʻa ke fakahā ʻiate ia ʻae ngaahi ngāue ʻae ʻOtua.
Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.
‌ʻOku totonu ke u fai ʻae ngaahi ngāue ʻo ia naʻa ne fekau au, lolotonga ʻene kei ʻaho: ʻoku haʻu ʻae pō, ʻoku ʻikai faʻa ngāue ai ha tokotaha.”
I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
‌ʻI heʻeku kei ʻi māmani ko e maama au ʻo māmani.
As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
Hili ʻene lea pehē, naʻe ʻaʻanu ia ki he kelekele, ʻo ne ngaohi ʻaki ʻae ʻaʻanu ʻae ʻumea, ʻo ne pani ʻaki ʻae ʻumea ʻae mata ʻoe tangata kui,
When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,
‌ʻO ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻAlu, ʻo kaukau ʻi he ano vai ko Seiloami,” (ʻa ia ko hono ʻuhinga, “Ko e fekau.”) Ko ia naʻe ʻalu ai ia, ʻo kaukau, pea haʻu kuo ʻā.
And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.
Ko ia ko e kaungāʻapi, pea mo kinautolu naʻe mamata muʻa kiate ia ʻi heʻene kui, naʻa nau pehē, “ʻIkai ko eni ia naʻe nofo ʻo kole?”
The neighbours therefore, and they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?
Pea tala ʻe he niʻihi, “Ko eni ia:” pea lea ʻae niʻihi, “ʻOku hangē ko ia:” ka naʻe pehē ʻe ia, “Ko au ia.”
Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he.
“Ko ia naʻa nau pehē kiate ia, naʻe fakaʻā fēfeeʻi ho mata?”
Therefore said they unto him, How were thine eyes opened?

Pea talaange ʻe ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko e tangata ʻoku ui ko Sisu naʻa ne ngaohi ʻae ʻumea, ʻo ne pani hoku mata, pea ne pehē kiate au, ‘ʻAlu ki he ano vai ko Seiloami, ʻo kaukau:’ pea naʻaku ʻalu, ʻo kaukau, pea u ʻā ai.”
He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.
Pea nau pehē ai kiate ia, “Kofaʻā ia?” Pea pehē ʻe ia, “ʻOku ʻikai te u ʻiloa.”
Then said they unto him, Where is he? He said, I know not.
Naʻa nau ʻomi ki he kau Fālesi ʻaia naʻe kui.
They brought to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind.
Pea ko e ʻaho Sāpate ʻaia naʻe ngaohi ai ʻe Sisu ʻae ʻumea, ʻo ne fakaʻā hono mata.
And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.
Pea fehuʻi foki ʻae kau Fālesi kiate ia, pe naʻe fēfē hono fakaʻā. Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, ‘Naʻe ʻai ʻe ia ʻae ʻumea ki hoku mata, pea u kaukau, pea ʻoku ou ʻā.”
Then again the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. He said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see.

Ko ia naʻe pehē ai ʻe he niʻihi ʻoe kau Fālesi, “ʻOku ʻikai mei he ʻOtua ʻae tangata ni, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai te ne tokanga ki he ʻaho Sāpate.” Pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, “ʻE faʻa fai fēfeeʻi ʻae ngaahi mana pehē ʻe ha angahala? Pea naʻa nau fakakikihi ai.”

Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them.
Pea naʻa nau toe fehuʻi ki he tangata kui, “Ko e hā hoʻo lau kiate ia, ʻi heʻene fakaʻā ho mata?” Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Ko e palōfita ia.”
They say unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, that he hath opened thine eyes? He said, He is a prophet.
Ka naʻe ʻikai tui ʻae kakai Siu naʻe kui ia, pea kuo ʻā, kaeʻoua ke nau ui ʻae mātuʻa ʻo ia kuo fakaʻā.
But the Jews did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight.
Pea nau fehuʻi kiate kinaua, ʻo pehē, “Ko hoʻomo tama eni, ʻoku mo lau naʻe fanauʻi kui? Pea ʻoku ʻa fēfē eni?”
And they asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? how then doth he now see?
Pea leaange ʻene mātuʻa kiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “ʻOku ma ʻilo ko ʻema tama eni, pea naʻe fanauʻi ʻoku kui:
His parents answered them and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:
Ka ko e meʻa ko ia ʻoku ʻā ai ni ia, ʻoku ʻikai te ma ʻilo; pea ʻoku ʻikai te ma ʻilo pe ko hai kuo fakaʻā hono mata; ka ʻoku lahi ia: fehuʻi ki ai: ke lea ia kiate ia.”
But by what means he now seeth, we know not; or who hath opened his eyes, we know not: he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself.
Naʻe pehē ʻae lea ʻa ʻene mātuʻa, he naʻa na manavahē ki he kakai Siu: he kuo alea pau ʻae kakai Siu, kapau ʻe ai ha tokotaha te ne fakahā ko e Kalaisi ia, ʻe kapusi ia mei he falelotu.
These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
Ko ia naʻe pehē ai ʻe heʻene mātuʻa, “ʻOku lahi ia; fehuʻi ki ai.”
Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.
Pea naʻa nau toe ui ʻae tangata naʻe kui, ʻonau pehē kiate ia, “Tuku ki he ʻOtua ʻae fakamālō: ʻoku mau ʻilo ko e angahala ʻae tangata ni.”
Then again called they the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give God the praise: we know that this man is a sinner.
Pea leaange ʻe ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko ha angahala ia pe ʻikai, ʻoku ʻikai te u ʻilo: ko e meʻa ʻe taha ʻoku ou ʻilo, naʻaku kui, ka ko eni ʻoku ou ʻā.”
He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
Pea toe fehuʻi ai ʻakinautolu kiate ia, “Ko e hā naʻa ne fai kiate koe? Naʻe fēfeeʻi ʻene fakaʻā ho mata?”
Then said they to him again, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?
Pea leaange ia kiate kinautolu, “Kuo ʻosi ʻeku tala kiate kimoutolu, pea ʻoku ʻikai te mou ongoʻi: ko e hā ʻoku mou toe fie fanongo ai? Te mou ului ko ʻene kau ākonga foki?”
He answered them, I have told you already, and ye did not hear: wherefore would ye hear it again? will ye also be his disciples?
Pea nau taukaea ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko ʻene ākonga ʻa koe; ka ko e kau ākonga ʻa Mōsese ʻakimautolu.
Then they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are Moses’ disciples.
‌ʻOku mau ʻilo naʻe folofola ʻae ʻOtua kia Mōsese: ka ko e tangata ni, ʻoku ʻikai te mau ʻilo pe ʻoku mei fē ia.”
We know that God spake unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is.
Pea leaange ʻae tangata, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ta ko e meʻa fakamanavahē eni, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai te mou ʻilo pe ʻoku haʻu ia mei fē, ka kuo ne fakaʻā hoku mata.
The man answered and said unto them, Why herein is a marvellous thing, that ye know not from whence he is, and yet he hath opened mine eyes.
‌ʻOku tau ʻilo ʻoku ʻikai ongoʻi ʻe he ʻOtua ʻae kau angahala: ka ʻoka lotu ha tangata ki he ʻOtua, pea fai hono finangalo, ʻoku ne ongoʻi ia.
Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.
Talu mei he kamataʻanga ʻo māmani ʻoku teʻeki fanongo naʻe ai ha tangata kuo fakaʻā ʻae mata ʻo ha tokotaha kuo fanauʻi kui.
Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind.
Ka ne ʻikai ʻi he ʻOtua ʻae tangata ni, ʻe ʻikai faʻa fai ʻe ia ha meʻa.”
If this man were not of God, he could do nothing.
Pea leaange ʻakinautolu, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Naʻa ke tupu tofu pe ʻi he ngaahi angahala, pea ʻoku ke akoʻi ʻakimautolu?” Pea naʻa nau kapusi ia kituʻa.
They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.
Pea ongoʻi ʻe Sisu kuo nau kapusi ia kituʻa: pea ne toki ʻilo ia, ʻo ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻOku ke tui ki he ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua?”
Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
Pea leaange ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻEiki, ko hai ia, koeʻuhi ke u tui kiate ia?”
He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?
Pea tala ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Kuo ke mamata kiate ia, pea ko ia ia ʻoku talanoa kiate koe.”
And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee.
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “ʻEiki, ʻoku ou tui. Pea naʻa ne hū kiate ia.
And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.
Pea lea ʻa Sisu, “Ko e meʻa ʻi he fakamaau kuo u haʻu ki māmani, koeʻuhi ko kinautolu ʻoku ʻikai mamata ke nau mamata; pea ke kui ʻakinautolu ʻoku mamata.”
And Jesus said, For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind.
Pea fanongo ki he ngaahi lea ni ʻae niʻihi ʻoe Fālesi naʻe ʻiate ia, ʻonau pehē ki ai, “ʻOku kui ʻakimautolu foki?”
And some of the Pharisees which were with him heard these words, and said unto him, Are we blind also?
Pea pehē ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Ka ne kui ʻakimoutolu, pehē, ʻe ʻikai haʻamou angahala ka ko eni ʻoku mou pehē, ʻOku mau ʻā ko ia ʻoku maʻu pe hoʻomou angahala.”
Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
“Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Ko ia ʻoku ʻikai hū ʻi he matapā ki he lotoʻā sipi, ka ʻoku kaka hake ʻi he hala kehe, ko e kaihaʻa ia mo e fakamālohi.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.
Ka ko ia ʻoku hū ʻi he matapā, ko e tauhi ia ʻoe fanga sipi.
But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
‌ʻOku toʻo kiate ia ʻe he leʻo; pea fanongo ki hono leʻo ʻae fanga sipi pea ʻoku ne ui ʻae sipi ʻaʻana ʻi honau hingoa ʻo ne tataki atu ʻakinautolu.
To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
Pea ka tuku atu ʻe ia ʻene sipi ʻaʻana ʻoku ʻalu muʻomuʻa ia ʻiate kinautolu, pea muimui ʻae sipi ʻiate ia: he ʻoku nau ʻilo hono leʻo.”
And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.
Pea ʻe ʻikai te nau muimui ʻi ha foʻou, ka te nau hola meiate ia: he ʻoku ʻikai te nau ʻilo ʻae leʻo ʻoe foʻou.
And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.
Naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe Sisu ʻae fakatātā ni kiate kinautolu: ka naʻe ʻikai te nau ʻilo hono ʻuhinga ʻo ʻene lea kiate kinautolu.
This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them.
Pea toe tala ai ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, Ko au ko e matapā ki he fanga sipi.
Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.
Ko kinautolu kotoa pē naʻe muʻomuʻa ʻiate au, ko e kau kaihaʻa mo e fakamālohi: ka naʻe ʻikai fanongo ʻae fanga sipi kiate kinautolu.
All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.
Ko au pe ko e matapā: pea ko ia ʻe hū ange ʻiate au, ʻe moʻui ia, pea ʻe feʻaluʻaki ai pe ia, ʻo maʻu ʻae meʻakai.
I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.
‌ʻOku ʻikai haʻu ʻae kaihaʻa, ka ke kaihaʻasi, pea ke tāmateʻi, pea ke fakaʻauha: kuo u haʻu au ke nau maʻu ʻae moʻui, pea ke nau maʻu ia ʻo lahi ʻaupito.
The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
“Ko au ko e tauhi lelei: ʻoku foaki ʻe he tauhi lelei ʻa ʻene moʻui koeʻuhi ko e fanga sipi.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.

Ka ko ia ʻoku unga ki he ngāue, ka ʻoku ʻikai ko e tauhi, ʻaia ʻoku ʻikai ʻaʻana ʻae fanga sipi, ʻoku mamata ia ʻoku haʻu ʻae ulofi, pea siʻaki ʻae fanga sipi, kae hola: pea moʻua ia ʻe he ulofi, ʻo fakahēʻi ʻae fanga sipi.
But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep.
‌ʻOku hola ʻae unga ngāue, koeʻuhi ko e unga ngāue pe ia, pea ʻoku ʻikai ʻofa ia ki he fanga sipi.
The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
Ko au ko e tauhi lelei; pea hangē ʻoku ʻilo au ʻe he Tamai, peau ʻilo foki ʻae Tamai,
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.
ʻOku pehē ʻa ʻeku ʻilo ʻaia ʻoku ʻaʻaku, mo e ʻilo au ʻekinautolu: pea ʻoku ou tuku hifo ʻeku moʻui koeʻuhi ko e fanga sipi.
As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep.
Pea ʻoku ai mo ʻeku fanga sipi kehe, ʻoku ʻikai ʻi he lotoʻā ko eni: te u ʻomi ʻakinautolu foki, pea te nau fanongo ki hoku leʻo; pea ʻe ai ʻae lotoʻā pe taha, mo e tauhi pe taha.”
And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.
Ko ia ʻoku ʻofa ai ʻa ʻeku Tamai kiate au, ko e meʻa ʻi heʻeku tuku hifo ʻeku moʻui, kau toe toʻo ia.
Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again.
‌ʻOku ʻikai ke toʻo ia ʻe ha taha ʻiate au, ka ʻoku ou tuku hifo ia ʻeau pe. ʻOku ou mafai ke tuku hifo ia, pea ʻoku ou mafai ke toe toʻo ia. Ko e fekau ni kuo u maʻu mei heʻeku Tamai.”
No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.
Pea naʻe toe fakakikihi ʻae kakai Siu, ko e meʻa ʻi he ngaahi lea ni.
There was a division therefore again among the Jews for these sayings.
Pea pehē ʻe honau tokolahi, “ʻOku ʻiate ia ha tēvolo, pea ʻoku faha; ko e hā ʻoku mou fanongo ai kiate ia?”
And many of them said, He hath a devil, and is mad; why hear ye him?
Pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, “ʻOku ʻikai ko e lea eni ʻa ha taha ʻoku ʻi ai ha tēvolo. ʻE mafai ʻe ha tēvolo ke fakaʻā ʻae mata ʻoe kui?”
Others said, These are not the words of him that hath a devil. Can a devil open the eyes of the blind?
Pea naʻe fai ʻi Selūsalema ʻae kātoanga ʻoe fakafoʻou, pea ko e faʻahitaʻu momoko.
And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.
Pea naʻe ʻeveʻeva ʻa Sisu ʻi he falelotu lahi, ʻi he fale hala ʻo Solomone.
And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.
Pea naʻe haʻu ʻae kakai Siu, ʻo kāpui ia, ʻonau pehē kiate ia, “ʻE fēfē hono fuoloa mo hoʻo taʻefakaʻilo kiate kimautolu? Kapau ko e Kalaisi koe, tala totonu mai kiate kimautolu.”
Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Naʻaku tala kiate kimoutolu, ka naʻe ʻikai te mou tui: ko e ngaahi ngāue ʻoku ou fai ʻi he huafa ʻo ʻeku Tamai, ʻoku fakamoʻoniʻi ai au.”
Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me.
Ka ʻoku ʻikai te mou tui, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ʻi heʻeku fanga sipi ʻakimoutolu.
But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.
‌ʻOku fanongo ʻeku fanga sipi ki hoku leʻo, ʻo hangē ko ʻeku tala kiate kimoutolu: pea ʻoku ou ʻiloa ʻakinautolu, pea ʻoku nau muimui ʻiate au:
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
Pea ʻoku ou foaki kiate kinautolu ʻae moʻui taʻengata; pea ʻe ʻikai ʻaupito te nau ʻauha, pe ʻe ʻikai ha taha te ne hamusi ʻakinautolu mei hoku nima.
And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
Ko ʻeku Tamai, ʻaia naʻa ne foaki mai kiate au, ʻoku lahi taha pe ia; pea ʻoku ʻikai ha tokotaha ʻoku faʻa hamusi mei he nima ʻo ʻeku Tamai.
My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand.
Ko au mo e Tamai ʻoku ma taha pe.
I and my Father are one.
Pea toe toʻo hake ʻe he kakai Siu ʻae maka, ke nau tolongaki ʻaki ia.
Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Kuo lahi ʻae ngāue lelei kuo u fakahā kiate kimoutolu mei heʻeku Tamai; ko e ngāue fē ia ʻoku mou tolongakiʻi ai au?
Jesus answered them, Many good works have I shewed you from my Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?
Pea talaange ʻe he kau Siu kiate ia, ʻo pehē, ʻOku ʻikai ko ha ngāue lelei ʻoku mau tolongakiʻi ai koe; ka ko e fie ʻOtua pe; koeʻuhi ko e tangata pe ʻa koe, ka ʻoku ke fai ke ʻOtua.”
The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone thee not; but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “ʻIkai kuo tohi ʻi hoʻomou fono, Ne u pehē, ‘Ko e ngaahi ʻotua ʻakimoutolu?’
Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods?
Kapau ʻoku ui ko e ʻotua ʻakinautolu naʻe folofola ki ai ʻae ʻOtua, pea ʻe ʻikai faʻa liʻaki ʻae tohi;
If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken;
‌ʻOku mou pehē kiate ia kuo fakatapui ʻe he Tamai, ʻo fekau ki māmani, ʻOku ke fie ʻOtua; koeʻuhi naʻaku pehē, Ko e ʻAlo au ʻoe ʻOtua?
Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?
Kapau ʻoku ʻikai te u fai ʻae ngāue ʻo ʻeku Tamai, ʻoua te mou tui kiate au.
If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.
Ka ʻi heʻeku fai ia, kapau ʻoku ʻikai te mou tui kiate au, tui ki he ngāue: koeʻuhi ke mou ʻilo, mo tui, ʻoku ʻiate au ʻae Tamai, mo au ʻiate ia.”
But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him.
Ko ia naʻa nau toe fie puke ai ia: ka naʻa ne fakahaofi ia mei honau nima,
Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand,
‌ʻO toe ʻalu ki he potu ʻituʻa Sioatani, ʻaia naʻe tomuʻa fai papitaiso ai ʻa Sione; pea nofo ai ia.
And went away again beyond Jordan into the place where John at first baptized; and there he abode.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ʻae tokolahi kiate ia, ʻonau pehē, “Naʻe ʻikai fai ʻe Sione ha mana: ka ko e meʻa kotoa pē naʻe lea ki ai ʻa Sione ki he tangata ni, ʻoku moʻoni.”
And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle: but all things that John spake of this man were true.
Pea naʻe tui ʻae tokolahi ʻi ai kiate ia.
And many believed on him there.
Pea naʻe mahaki ʻa Lasalosi, ko e tangata ʻe tokotaha ʻi Pētani, ko e kolo ʻa Mele mo hono tokoua ko Māʻata.
Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
(Ko e Mele ko ia ia naʻa ne tākai ʻae ʻEiki ʻaki ʻae lolo, ʻo ne holoholo hono vaʻe ʻaki hono louʻulu, naʻe mahaki hono tuongaʻane ko Lasalosi.)
(It was that Mary which anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.)
Ko ia naʻe fekau ai ʻe hono ongo tuofefine kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “ʻEiki, vakai, ko ia ʻoku ke ʻofa ai ʻoku mahaki.”
Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
Pea kuo fanongo ʻa Sisu, pea ne pehē, “ʻOku ʻikai ko e mahaki eni ke mate ai, ka ke ongoongolelei ai ʻae ʻOtua, pea ke ongoongolelei ai ʻae ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua.”
When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby.
Pea naʻe ʻofa ʻa Sisu kia Māʻata, mo hono tehina, mo Lasalosi.
Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
Pea kuo fanongo ia ki heʻene mahaki, naʻa ne kei nofo ʻi he potu ko ia ʻo ʻaho ua.
When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was.
Hili ia, pea pehē ʻe ia ki he kau ākonga, “Ke tau toe ʻalu ki Siutea.”
Then after that saith he to his disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.
Pea tala ʻe he kau ākonga kiate ia, “Lāpai, naʻe toki kumi ʻe he kau Siu ke tolongaki koe ʻaki ʻae maka; pea ʻoku ke toe ʻalu ki ai?”
His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?
Pea pehēange ʻe Sisu, “ʻIkai ʻoku hongofulu ma ua ʻae feituʻulaʻā ʻi he ʻaho? Kapau ʻoku ʻeveʻeva ha tangata ʻi he ʻaho, ʻoku ʻikai tūkia ia, koeʻuhi ʻoku mamata ia ki he maama ʻoe māmani.
Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
Pea kapau ʻoku ʻeveʻeva ha tangata ʻi he poʻuli, ʻoku tūkia ia, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ha maama ʻi ai.”
But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no light in him.
Naʻe hili ʻene lea ni, pea toki pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko hotau kāinga ko Lasalosi ʻoku mohe; ka ʻoku ou ʻalu, koeʻuhi ke u fafangu ia mei he mohe.”
These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
Pea pehē ai ʻe heʻene kau ākonga, “ʻEiki, kapau ʻoku mohe, ʻe lelei ai ia.”
Then said his disciples, Lord, if he sleep, he shall do well.
Naʻe lea ʻa Sisu ki heʻene mate ka naʻa nau mahalo ko ʻene lea ki he mālōlō ʻi he mohe.
Howbeit Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep.
Pea toki tala fakatotonu ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Kuo mate ʻa Lasalosi.
Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.
Pea ʻoku ou fiefia ʻi he ʻikai te u ʻi ai, koeʻuhi ko kimoutolu, koeʻuhi ke mou tui; ka tau ō kiate ia.”
And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.
Pea lea ai ʻa Tōmasi, ʻoku ui ko Titimasi, ki heʻene kaungā ākonga, “Ke tau ō foki, ka tau mate mo ia.”
Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
Pea kuo ʻalu atu ʻa Sisu, pea ne ʻilo kuo ʻaho fā hono tuku ia ki he faʻitoka.
Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.
Pea naʻe ofi ʻa Pētani ki Selūsalema, ko e maile ʻe ua nai hono mamaʻo.
Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off:
Pea haʻu ʻae kau Siu tokolahi kia Māʻata mo Mele, ke fakafiemālieʻi ʻakinaua koeʻuhi ko hona tuongaʻane.
And many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother.
Pea ʻi he fanongo ʻe Māʻata ʻoku haʻu ʻa Sisu, naʻa ne ʻalu ʻo fakafetaulaki kiate ia: ka naʻe nofo pe ʻa Mele ʻi he fale.
Then Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary sat still in the house.
Pea lea ai ʻa Māʻata kia Sisu, ʻEiki, ka ne ke ʻi heni, pehē, ne ʻikai mate hoku tuongaʻane.
Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
Ka ʻoku ou ʻilo ʻa eni, ko ia kotoa pē te ke kolea ki he ʻOtua, ʻe foaki ʻe he ʻOtua kiate koe.”
But I know, that even now, whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “ʻE toetuʻu ho tuongaʻane.”
Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.
Pea tala ʻe Māʻata kiate ia, “ʻOku ou ʻilo ʻe toetuʻu ia ʻi he toetuʻu ʻi he ʻaho fakamui.”
Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Ko au ko e toetuʻu, mo e moʻui: ko ia ʻoku tui kiate au, ka ne mate ia, ʻe moʻui pe ia:
Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
Pea ko ia ʻoku moʻui mo tui kiate au, ʻe ʻikai ʻaupito mate ia. ʻOku ke tui ki ai?”
And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
Pea ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻIo, ʻEiki: ʻoku ou tui ko e Kalaisi ʻa koe, ko e ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua, ʻaia naʻe totonu ke haʻu ki māmani.”
She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.
Pea hili ʻene lea ko ia, naʻe ʻalu ia, ʻo ne ui fakafufū hono tehina ko Mele, ʻo ne pehē, Kuo haʻu ʻae Akonaki, pea ʻoku fehuʻi kiate koe.”
And when she had so said, she went her way, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Master is come, and calleth for thee.
Pea ʻi heʻene ongoʻi ia, naʻa ne tuʻu hake leva, ʻo haʻu kiate ia.
As soon as she heard that, she arose quickly, and came unto him.
Pea kuo teʻeki hoko ʻa Sisu ki he kolo, ka naʻe ʻi he potu ko ia naʻe fakafetaulaki ai ʻa Māʻata kiate ia.
Now Jesus was not yet come into the town, but was in that place where Martha met him.

Pea ko e kau Siu naʻe ʻiate ia ʻi he fale, ʻonau fakafiemālieʻi ia, ʻi heʻenau vakai ʻoku tuʻu fakavave ʻa Mele, ʻo ʻalu kituʻa, naʻa nau muimui ai, ʻonau pehē, ʻOku ʻalu ia ki he faʻitoka ke tangi ai.
The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave to weep there.
Pea kuo ʻalu ange ʻa Mele ki he potu ʻoku ʻi ai ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne mamata ki ai, pea tōmapeʻe ia ki hono vaʻe, ʻo ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ka ne ke ʻi heni, pehē, ne ʻikai mate hoku tuongaʻane.”
Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
Pea ʻi he mamata ʻa Sisu kiate ia ʻoku tangi, pea tangi foki mo e kakai Siu naʻe haʻu mo ia, pea toʻe ia ʻi he laumālie, pea mamahi ia,
When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,
‌ʻO ne pehē, “Kuo mou tuku ʻi fē ia? Pea nau tala kiate ia, ʻEiki, haʻu ʻo mamata.”
And said, Where have ye laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see.
Pea tangi ʻa Sisu.
Jesus wept.
Pea lea ai ʻae kau Siu, “Vakai ki hono lahi ʻo ʻene ʻofa kiate ia.”
Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!
Pea lea ʻa honau niʻihi, “ʻIkai ʻe mafai ʻe he tangata ni, ʻoku ne fakaʻā ʻae mata ʻoe kui, ke taʻofi ke ʻoua naʻa mate ʻae tangata ni?”
And some of them said, Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?
Pea ko ia naʻe toʻetoʻe ʻa Sisu ʻi hono loto, pea ʻalu atu ki he tanuʻanga. Ko e ʻana ia pea naʻe tāpuni ʻaki ia ʻae maka.
Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
Pea tala ʻe Sisu, “Mou toʻo ʻae maka.” Pea lea kiate ia ʻa Māʻata, ko e tuofefine ʻo ia kuo mate, ʻEiki, kuo namuhāhā: he ko hono ʻaho fā eni.
Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.
Pea lea ʻa Sisu kiate ia, “ʻIkai naʻaku tala kiate koe, kapau te ke tui, te ke mamata ki he māfimafi ʻoe ʻOtua?”
Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?
Pea naʻa nau toʻo ʻae maka mei he potu naʻe tuku ai ʻae mate. Pea hanga hake ʻae fofonga ʻo Sisu, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻE Tamai, ʻoku ou fakafetaʻi kuo ke ongoʻi au.
Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
Pea ʻoku ou ʻilo ʻoku ke ongoʻi maʻu aipē au: ka ko e meʻa ʻi he kakai ʻoku tutuʻu ni, ko ia kuo u lea ai, koeʻuhi ke nau tui naʻa ke fekau au.”
And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.
Pea hili ʻene lea pehē, pea lea leʻo lahi ia, “Lasalosi, tuʻu mai.”
And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
Pea naʻe tuʻu mai ʻaia naʻe mate, kuo haʻihaʻi hono nima mo e vaʻe ʻaki ʻae kofu tanu: pea kuo nonoʻo ʻaki hono mata ʻae holoholo. Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “Vevete, ʻo tukuange ia.”
And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
Pea ko e tokolahi ʻoe kau Siu naʻe haʻu kia Mele, hili ʻenau mamata ki he ngāue naʻe fai ʻe Sisu, naʻa nau tui kiate ia.
Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.
Ka naʻe ʻalu honau niʻihi ki he kau Fālesi, ʻo tala kiate kinautolu ʻae ngaahi meʻa kuo fai ʻe Sisu.
But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.
Pea fakataha ʻe he kau taulaʻeiki lahi mo e kau Fālesi ʻae kau fakamaau, ʻonau pehē, “Ko e hā ʻoku tau fai? He ʻoku fai ʻe he tangata ni ʻae ngaahi mana lahi.
Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles.
Kapau te tau tuku noa ai pe ia, ʻe tui kotoa pē kiate ia: pea ʻe haʻu ʻae kakai Loma, ʻo fakaʻauha hotau potu mo hotau puleʻanga.”
If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.
Pea ko honau tokotaha, ko Kaiafasi, ko e taulaʻeiki lahi ia ʻi he taʻu ko ia, naʻe pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻikai te mou ʻilo ha meʻa,
And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,
Pea tokanga ʻe lelei kiate kitautolu, ke mate ha tangata ʻe tokotaha maʻae kakai, kaeʻoua naʻa ʻauha ʻae puleʻanga kotoa.”
Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.
Pea naʻe ʻikai meiate ia ʻene lea ko ia: ka ko e taulaʻeiki lahi ia ʻi he taʻu ko ia, pea ne kikite ʻe mate ʻa Sisu ki he puleʻanga ko ia;
And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation;
Pea ʻoku ʻikai ki he puleʻanga pe ko ia, ka koeʻuhi ke ne tānaki ʻo fakataha ʻae fānau ʻae ʻOtua kuo fakahēʻi mamaʻo.
And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.
Pea talu mei he ʻaho ko ia naʻa nau alea fakataha ke tāmateʻi ia.
Then from that day forth they took counsel together for to put him to death.
Ko ia naʻe ʻikai toe ʻalu fakahā ʻa Sisu ʻi he kakai Siu; ka naʻe mahuʻi ia mei ai ki he fonua ofi ki he toafa, ki he kolo naʻe ui ko ʻEfalemi, pea nofo ai mo ʻene kau ākonga.
Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews; but went thence unto a country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there continued with his disciples.
Pea kuo ofi ʻa e kātoanga ʻoe Lakaatu ʻae kakai Siu: naʻe ʻalu hake ʻae tokolahi mei he tukuʻuta ki Selūsalema, ʻi he teʻeki hoko ʻae kātoanga ke fakamaʻa ʻakinautolu.
And the Jews’ passover was nigh at hand: and many went out of the country up to Jerusalem before the passover, to purify themselves.
Pea naʻa nau kumi ʻa Sisu, ʻonau fealēleaʻaki, ʻi heʻenau tutuʻu ʻi he falelotu lahi, “Ko e hā hoʻomou mahalo? ʻE ʻikai te ne haʻu ki he kātoanga?”
Then sought they for Jesus, and spake among themselves, as they stood in the temple, What think ye, that he will not come to the feast?
He kuo fekau ʻe he kau taulaʻeiki lahi, mo e Fālesi, kapau kuo ʻilo ʻe ha tangata pe ʻoku ʻi fē ia, ke ne fakahā, ka nau puke ia.
Now both the chief priests and the Pharisees had given a commandment, that, if any man knew where he were, he should shew it, that they might take him.
Pea toe ono ʻae ʻaho pea fai ʻae kātoanga ʻoe Lakaatu, pea haʻu ʻa Sisu ki Pētani, naʻe ʻi ai ʻa Lasalosi ʻaia naʻe fokotuʻu ʻe ia mei he mate.
Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.
Pea naʻa nau te u ai kiate ia ʻae ʻohomohe: pea tauhi ʻe Māʻata: ka ko e tokotaha ʻa Lasalosi ʻokinautolu naʻe nofo mo ia ʻi he keinangaʻanga.
There they made him a supper; and Martha served: but Lazarus was one of them that sat at the table with him.

Pea toʻo ʻe Mele ʻae lolo ko e naʻati moʻoni, ko e lau taha hono mamafa, ko e koloa lahi, ʻo ne tākai ʻaki ʻae vaʻe ʻo Sisu, ʻo holoholo ʻaki hono vaʻe ʻa hono louʻulu: pea naʻe pito ʻae fale ʻi he namu lelei ʻoe lolo.
Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
Pea lea ai ʻae tokotaha ʻo ʻene ākonga, ko Siutasi ʻIsikaliote, ko e foha ʻo Saimone, ʻaia ʻe lavakiʻi ia,
Then saith one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, which should betray him,
“Ko e hā naʻe ʻikai fakatau ai ʻae lolo ni ʻaki ʻae tenali ʻe tolungeau, pea foaki ki he masiva?”
Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?
Naʻa ne lea ʻaki eni, ka naʻe ʻikai ko ʻene tokanga ki he masiva; ka koeʻuhi ko e kaihaʻa ia, pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae kato, ʻo ne fua ʻaia naʻe tuku ki ai.
This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.
Pea lea ai ʻa Sisu, “Tuku ai pe ia: kuo tauhi ʻe ia ʻae meʻa ni ki he ʻaho ʻo hoku tanu.
Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this.
He ʻoku ʻiate kimoutolu maʻuaipē ʻae masiva; ka ʻoku ʻikai teu ʻiate kimoutolu maʻuaipē au.”
For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.
Pea naʻe ʻilo ʻe he tokolahi ʻoe kakai Siu ʻoku ʻi ai ia: pea naʻa nau haʻu, ka naʻe ʻikai koeʻuhi ko Sisu pe, ka koeʻuhi ke nau mamata kia Lasalosi foki, ʻaia naʻa ne fokotuʻu mei he mate.
Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.
Ka naʻe alea ʻae kau taulaʻeiki lahi, ke nau tāmateʻi ʻa Lasalosi foki;
But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;
Koeʻuhi ko e meʻa ʻiate ia naʻe mahuʻi ʻae tokolahi ʻoe kau Siu, ʻo tui kia Sisu.
Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.
ʻI he ʻaho naʻa na feholoi, naʻe fanongo ʻae kakai tokolahi kuo haʻu ki he kātoanga, ʻoku haʻu ʻa Sisu ki Selūsalema,
On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
Naʻa nau toʻo mai ʻae ngaahi vaʻa ponga, ʻonau ʻalu atu ke fakafetaulaki kiate ia, ʻonau kalanga, “Hosana: ʻOku monūʻia ʻae Tuʻi ʻo ʻIsileli, ʻoku hāʻele mai ʻi he huafa ʻo Sihova.”
Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
Pea kuo maʻu ʻe Sisu ʻae ʻasi mui, naʻa ne heka ai; ʻo hangē ko ia kuo tohi,
And Jesus, when he had found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,
“ʻE taʻahine ʻo Saione, ʻoua ʻe manavahē: vakai, ʻoku haʻu ho Tuʻi, ʻoku heka ki he ʻuhikiʻi ʻasi.”
Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.
Ko e ngaahi meʻa ni, naʻe ʻikai tomuʻa ʻilo ʻe heʻene kau ākonga; ka ʻi he hakeakiʻi ʻa Sisu, naʻa nau manatu ai kuo tohi ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kiate ia, pea kuo nau fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kiate ia.
These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.
Pea naʻe fakamoʻoni ʻae kakai ko ia naʻe ʻiate ia ʻi heʻene ui ʻa Lasalosi mei he tanuʻanga, ʻo ne fokotuʻu ia mei he mate.
The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.
Ko ia naʻe fakafetaulaki ai ʻae kakai kiate ia, he naʻa nau fanongo kuo ne fai ʻae mana ni.
For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle.
Pea ko ia naʻe alea ai ʻae kau Fālesi ʻiate kinautolu, ʻIkai te mou vakai ʻoku ʻikai ʻaupito te mou lavaʻi ha meʻa? “Vakai, kuo muimui ʻae kakai kotoa pē ʻiate ia.”
The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.
Pea naʻe ai ʻae kau Kiliki niʻihi ʻiate kinautolu naʻe ʻalu hake ke hū ʻi he kātoanga.
And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast:
Pea naʻa nau haʻu kia Filipe, ʻaia naʻe ʻo Petesaita ʻi Kāleli, ʻonau kole kiate ia, ʻo pehē, ʻEiki, ʻoku mau fie mamata kia Sisu.
The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ʻa Filipe ʻo tala kia ʻAnitelū: pea toe tala kia Sisu ʻe ʻAnitelū mo Filipe.
Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: and again Andrew and Philip tell Jesus.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu kiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Kuo hokosia ʻae ʻaho, ke fakaongoongolelei ai ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata.
And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.
Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Kapau ʻoku ʻikai mokulu ʻae tengaʻi uite ki he kelekele pea mate, ʻoku nofo taha ai pe: ka ʻi heʻene mate, ʻoku tupu mei ai ʻae fua lahi.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
Ko ia ʻoku ʻofa ki heʻene moʻui, ʻe mole ia ʻiate ia; pea ko ia ʻoku fehiʻa ki heʻene moʻui ʻi he māmani, te ne maʻu ia ki he moʻui taʻengata.
He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.
Kapau ʻoku tauhi au ʻe ha tangata, tuku ke ne muimui ʻiate au; pea ko e potu teu ʻi ai, ʻe ʻi ai foki ʻa ʻeku tamaioʻeiki: kapau ʻoku tauhi au ʻe ha tangata, ʻe fakaongoongolelei ia ʻe he Tamai.
If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour.
“Ko eni kuo mamahi hoku laumālie; pea ko e hā ʻeku lea? Te u pehē, ʻE Tamai, fakamoʻui au mei he ʻaho ni? Ka naʻaku haʻu koeʻuhi ke u hokosia ʻae ʻaho ni.
Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour.
‌ʻE Tamai, fakaongoongolelei ho huafa.” Pea naʻe hoko mai ʻae leʻo ni mei he langi, “Kuo u fakaongoongolelei ia, pea te u toe fakaongoongolelei ia.”
Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.
Pea ko ia naʻe pehē ai ʻe he kakai naʻe tutuʻu ai, mo ongoʻi ia, ko e mana: pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, “Ko e ʻāngelo ʻoku lea kiate ia.”
The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him.
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne pehē, “Naʻe ʻikai ongo mai ʻae leʻo ni koeʻuhi ko au, ka koeʻuhi ko kimoutolu.
Jesus answered and said, This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes.
Ko eni ʻae fakamaau ʻoe māmani ʻe kapusi eni ʻae ʻeiki ʻoe māmani kituaʻā,
Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
Pea kapau ʻe hiki au ki ʻolunga mei he fonua, te u tohoaki ʻae kakai kotoa pē kiate au.”
And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.
Ko ʻene lea pehē, ko e fakahā ʻae mateʻanga ko ia ʻe mate ai ia.
This he said, signifying what death he should die.
Pea leaange ʻae kakai kiate ia, “Kuo mau fanongo mei he fono ʻoku nofo ʻae Kalaisi ʻo taʻengata: pea ʻoku fēfē hoʻo lau, ʻE hiki hake ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata? ʻE fēfē nai ʻae Foha ko ia ʻoe tangata?
The people answered him, We have heard out of the law that Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?

Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “ʻE toetoe siʻi pe ʻene ʻiate kimoutolu ʻae maama. ʻEveʻeva lolotonga hoʻomou maʻu ʻae maama telia naʻa tō ʻae poʻuli kiate kimoutolu: he ko ia ʻoku ʻeveʻeva ʻi he poʻuli, ʻoku ʻikai ʻilo ʻe ia pe ko ʻene ʻalu ki fē.
Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.
‌ʻI hoʻomou kei maʻu ʻae maama, tui ki he maama, koeʻuhi ke mou hoko ko e fānau ʻae maama.” Naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe Sisu ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, pea ʻalu, ʻo ne fufū ia ʻiate kinautolu.
While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.
He kuo fai ʻe ia ʻae ngaahi mana lahi ʻi honau ʻao, ka naʻe ʻikai te nau tui kiate ia:
But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:
Pea naʻe fakamoʻoni ai ʻae lea ʻae palōfita ko ʻIsaia, ʻaia naʻe pehē, “ʻEiki, ko hai kuo tui ki heʻemau fakaongoongoa? Pea kuo fakahā kia hai ʻae nima ʻo Sihova?”
That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
Ko ia naʻe ʻikai ai te nau faʻa tui, he naʻe toe tala foki ʻe ʻIsaia,
Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again,
“Kuo fakakui ʻe ia honau mata, ʻo fakafefeka honau loto; ke ʻoua naʻa nau vakai ʻaki honau mata, pe ʻilo ʻaki honau loto, pea liliu, peau fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu.”
He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.
Ko e ngaahi meʻa ni naʻe lea ʻaki ʻe ʻIsaia, ʻi heʻene mamata ki hono nāunau, pea ne lea kiate ia.
These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him.
Pea naʻe tui kiate ia ʻae tokolahi ʻi he kau pule foki; ka ko e meʻa ʻi he kau Fālesi, naʻe ʻikai te nau fakahā ia, telia naʻa kapusi ʻakinautolu mei he falelotu:
Nevertheless among the chief rulers also many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue:
He naʻe lahi ʻenau manako ki he fakamālō ʻae tangata ʻi he fakamālō ʻae ʻOtua.
For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.
Pea kalanga ʻa Sisu ʻo pehē, “Ko ia ʻoku tui kiate au, ʻoku ʻikai tui kiate au pe, ka kiate ia naʻa ne fekau au.
Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.
Pea ko ia ʻoku ne mamata kiate au, ʻoku ne mamata kiate ia naʻa ne fekau au.
And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me.
Kuo u haʻu au ko e maama ki māmani, koeʻuhi ko ia ʻe tui kiate au ke ʻoua naʻa nofo ia ʻi he poʻuli.
I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness.
Pea kapau ʻoku fanongo ha tangata ki heʻeku ngaahi lea, kae ʻikai tui, ʻoku ʻikai te u fakamaauʻi ia: he naʻe ʻikai te u haʻu ke fakamaauʻi ʻa māmani, ka ke fakamoʻui ʻa māmani.
And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
Ko ia ʻoku ne liʻaki au ʻo ʻikai maʻu ʻeku ngaahi lea, ʻoku ai ha taha ʻoku fakamaauʻi ia: ko e lea kuo u lea ʻaki, ko ia te ne fakamaauʻi ia ʻi he ʻaho fakamui.
He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.
He naʻe ʻikai te u lea ʻiate au; ka ko e Tamai naʻa ne fekau au, kuo ne puleʻi au ʻi he meʻa te u fekau, mo ia te u lea ʻaki.
For I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.
Pea ʻoku ou ʻilo ko ʻene fekau ko e moʻui taʻengata: ko ia ko e meʻa ʻoku ou lea ʻaki, ʻoku ou lea ʻaki ʻo hangē ko e fekau ʻae Tamai kiate au.”
And I know that his commandment is life everlasting: whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak.

Pea ʻi he teʻeki fai ʻae kātoanga ʻoe Lakaatu, naʻe ʻilo ʻe Sisu kuo hoko hono ʻaho ke ʻalu ai ʻi he māmani ki he Tamai, pea naʻe ʻofa ia kiate kinautolu naʻe ʻaʻana ʻoku ʻi he māmani, pea ʻofa pe ia ki ai ʻo aʻu ki he ngataʻanga.

Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
Pea lolotonga ʻae ʻohomohe, kuo tomuʻa ʻai ʻe he tēvolo ki he loto ʻo Siutasi ʻIsikaliote, ko e foha ʻo Saimone, ke ne lavakiʻi ia;
And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him;
Pea kuo ʻilo ʻe Sisu kuo tuku ʻe he Tamai ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē ki hono nima, pea naʻe haʻu ia mei he ʻOtua, pea ʻoku ʻalu ki he ʻOtua;
Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he was come from God, and went to God;
Naʻe tuʻu hake ia mei he ʻohomohe, ʻo tuku hono kofu; pea toʻo ʻae holoholo, ʻo nonoʻo ia.
He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.
Pea toki lilingi ʻe ia ʻae vai ki he kumete, pea ne kamata fufulu ʻae vaʻe ʻoe kau ākonga, pea holoholo ʻaki ʻae holo naʻe nonoʻo ʻaki.
After that he poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.
Pea haʻu ai ia kia Saimone Pita: pea pehē ʻe Pita kiate ia, “ʻEiki, te ke fufulu hoku vaʻe?”
Then cometh he to Simon Peter: and Peter saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Ko ia ʻoku ou fai, ʻoku ʻikai te ke ʻilo ni; ka te ke ʻilo ʻamui.”
Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter.
Pea pehē ʻe Pita kiate ia, “ʻE ʻikai ʻaupito te ke fufulu hoku vaʻe.” Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Ka ʻikai te u fufulu koe, pea ʻe ʻikai te ke kau mo au.”
Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
Pea pehē ʻe Saimone Pita kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ʻikai ko hoku vaʻe pē, ka ko hoku nima mo hoku ʻulu.”
Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Ko ia kuo kaukau, ʻoku ʻikai ʻaonga ke fufulu ka ko hono vaʻe pē, he ʻoku maʻa kotoa pē ia: pea ʻoku maʻa ʻakimoutolu, kae ʻikai kotoa pē.”
Jesus saith to him, He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
He naʻa ne ʻilo ʻaia te ne lavaki ia; ko ia naʻe pehē ai ʻe ia, “ʻOku ʻikai te mou maʻa kotoa pē.”
For he knew who should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.
Pea hili ʻene kaukau honau vaʻe, naʻe ʻai hono ngaahi kofu, pea toe nofo hifo, pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku mou ʻilo ʻaia kuo u fai kiate kimoutolu?”
So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?
“ʻOku mou ui au ko e Takimuʻa mo e ʻEiki: pea ko hoʻomou lea totonu ia; he ko au ia.
Ye call me Master and Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.
Pea kapau ko au, ko e ʻEiki mo e Takimuʻa, kuo u fufulu homou vaʻe; ʻoku totonu hoʻomou fetoutou fefufuluʻaki homou vaʻe.
If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.
He kuo u tuku kiate kimoutolu ʻae fakatātā, koeʻuhi ke mou fai ʻo tatau mo ia kuo u fai kiate kimoutolu.
For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, ʻOku ʻikai lahi ʻae tamaioʻeiki ki heʻene ʻeiki; pea ʻoku ʻikai lahi ʻaia kuo fekauʻi ʻiate ia naʻa ne fekau ia.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.
‌ʻOku mou monūʻia ʻi hoʻomou ʻilo ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni, ʻo kapau te mou fai ki ai.
If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
“ʻOku ʻikai kau ʻeku lea kiate kimoutolu kotoa pē: ʻoku ou ʻilo ʻaia kuo u fili: ka koeʻuhi ke fakamoʻoni ʻae tohi, ‘Ko ia ʻoku kai mā mo au, kuo hiki hono vaʻe kiate au.’
I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.
Pea ko eni ʻoku ou tala ia kiate kimoutolu ʻi he teʻeki ai hoko, koeʻuhi ʻoka hoko ia, ke mou tui ‘ko au ia.’
Now I tell you before it come, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he.
Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Ko ia ʻoku ne maʻu ʻaia ʻoku ou fekau, ʻoku ne maʻu au; pea ko ia ʻoku ne maʻu au, ʻoku ne maʻu ʻaia naʻa ne fekauʻi au.”
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
Pea hili ʻae lea ko ia ʻa Sisu, pea mamahi ia ʻi hono laumālie, ʻo ne fakahā, ʻo pehē, Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, “ʻE lavakiʻi au ʻe homou tokotaha.”
When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
Pea fesiofaki ʻae kau ākonga kiate kinautolu, ʻonau fifili pe ko ʻene lea kia hai.
Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.
Pea naʻe faʻaki ki he fatafata ʻo Sisu ʻene ākonga ʻe tokotaha, naʻe ʻofa ai ʻa Sisu.
Now there was leaning on Jesus’ bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
Ko ia naʻe kamokamo ai ʻe Saimone Pita kiate ia, koeʻuhi ke ne fehuʻi pe ko hai ia kuo ne lea ki ai.
Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spake.
Pea lea falala ʻe ia ki he fatafata ʻo Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ko hai ia?”
He then lying on Jesus’ breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu, “Ko ia ia te u ʻatu ki ai ʻae konga mā hili ʻeku peke ia.” Pea hili ʻene peke ʻae konga, ne ne ʻatu ia kia Siutasi ʻIsikaliote, ko e foha ʻo Saimone.
Jesus answered, He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
Pea hili ʻae peke, pea hū ʻa Sētane kiate ia. Pea pehē ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Ko ia ʻoku ke fai, fai vave.”
And after the sop Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus unto him, That thou doest, do quickly.
Pea naʻe ʻikai ʻilo ʻe ha tokotaha ʻi he keinangaʻanga pe ko e hā ʻoku pehē ai ʻene lea kiate ia.
Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him.
He naʻe mahalo ʻae niʻihi, ko e meʻa ʻi he maʻu ʻe Siutasi ʻae kato, naʻe tala ʻe Sisu kiate ia, Fakatau ʻaia ʻoku tau masiva ai ki he kātoanga; pe, koeʻuhi ke ne foaki ha meʻa ki he masiva.
For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.
Pea maʻu ʻe ia ʻae peke, ʻo ʻalu leva kituaʻā: pea kuo poʻuli.
He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night.
Pea kuo ʻalu ia kituaʻā, pea lea ʻa Sisu, “Ko eni kuo fakaongoongolelei ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata, pea ʻoku fakaongoongolelei ʻae ʻOtua ʻiate ia.
Therefore, when he was gone out, Jesus said, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.
Kapau ʻoku fakaongoongolelei ʻae ʻOtua ʻiate ia, ʻe fakaongoongolelei ia ʻe he ʻOtua ʻiate ia, pea te ne fakaongoongolelei leva ia.
If God be glorified in him, God shall also glorify him in himself, and shall straightway glorify him.

‌ʻAe fānau ʻofeina, ʻoku toe siʻi pē ʻeku ʻiate kimoutolu. Te mou kumi au: pea hangē ko ʻeku tala ki he kakai Siu, ‘Ko e potu ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai, ʻe ʻikai te mou faʻa hoko ki ai;’ ʻoku pehē ni ʻeku lea kiate kimoutolu.
Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say to you.
‌ʻOku ou tuku ʻae fekau foʻou kiate kimoutolu, Koeʻuhi ke mou feʻofaʻaki kiate kimoutolu; pea hangē ko ʻeku ʻofa kiate kimoutolu, ke mou feʻofaʻaki foki kiate kimoutolu.
A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
‌ʻI he meʻa ni ʻe ʻilo ai ʻe he kakai kotoa pē ko ʻeku kau ākonga ʻakimoutolu, ʻo kapau te mou feʻofaʻaki kiate kimoutolu.”
By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
Pea lea ʻa Saimone Pita kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ʻoku ke ʻalu ki fē?” Pea talaange ʻe Sisu ki ai, “Ko ia ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai, ʻoku ʻikai te ke faʻa muimui ni ʻiate au; ka te ke muimui ʻiate au ʻamui.”
Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
Pea fehuʻi ʻe Pita kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ko e hā ʻe ʻikai te u muimui ai ni kiate koe? Te u tuku hifo ʻeku moʻui koeʻuhi ko koe.”
Peter said unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thy sake.
Pea pehēange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Te ke tuku koā hoʻo moʻui koeʻuhi ko au? Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate koe, ʻE ʻikai ʻuʻua ʻae moa, kae tuʻo tolu haʻo fakafisi kiate au.
Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for my sake? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.
“ʻOua naʻa mamahi homou loto: ʻoku mou tui ki he ʻOtua, tui foki kiate au.
Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
‌ʻI he fale ʻo ʻeku Tamai ʻoku ai ʻae ngaahi nofoʻanga ʻoku lahi: ka ne ʻikai, pehē kuo u tala ia kiate kimoutolu. ʻOku ou ʻalu ke teuteu ha potu moʻomoutolu.
In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
Pea kapau teu ʻalu, ʻo teuteu ha potu moʻomoutolu, te u toe haʻu, ʻo maʻu ʻakimoutolu kiate au; koeʻuhi ko e potu te u ʻi ai, te mou ʻi ai foki.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
Pea ko e potu ʻoku ou ʻalu ki ai ʻoku mou ʻilo, pea ʻoku mou ʻilo mo e hala.”
And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know.
Pea lea ʻa Tōmasi kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ʻoku ʻikai te mau ʻilo pe ʻoku ke ʻalu ki fē; pea ʻe fēfē ʻemau ʻilo ʻae hala?”
Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?
Pea talaange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Ko au ko e hala, mo e moʻoni, pea mo e moʻui: ʻoku ʻikai haʻu ha tangata ʻe taha ki he Tamai, kae ʻiate au.
Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
Ka ne mou ʻilo au, pehē, kuo mou ʻilo mo ʻeku Tamai foki: pea ngata mei heni ʻoku mou ʻilo ia, pea kuo mou mamata kiate ia.”
If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
Pea lea ʻa Filipe kiate ia, “ʻEiki, fakahā kiate kimautolu ʻae Tamai pea mau fiemālie ai.”
Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.

Pea pehēange ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “Filipe, he kuo pehē ni hono fuoloa ʻo ʻeku ʻiate kimoutolu, ka ʻoku teʻeki ai te ke ʻilo au? Ko ia kuo ne mamata kiate au, kuo mamata ia ki he Tamai; pea fēfē ai haʻo pehē, ‘Fakahā kiate kimautolu ʻae Tamai?’
Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?

‌ʻOku ʻikai te ke tui ʻoku ou ʻi he Tamai, mo e Tamai ʻiate au? Ko e lea ʻoku ou leaʻaki kiate kimoutolu, ʻoku ʻikai te u lea ʻaki ʻiate au: ka ko e Tamai, ʻoku nofo ʻiate au, ʻoku ne fai ʻae ngaahi ngāue.
Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works.
Tui mai kiate au ʻoku ou ʻi he Tamai, mo e Tamai ʻiate au: pea kapau ʻe ʻikai, pea tui kiate au koeʻuhi ko e ngaahi ngāue.
Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works’ sake.

Ko e moʻoni, ko e moʻoni, ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, Ko ia ʻoku tui kiate au, ko e ngaahi ngāue ʻoku ou fai ʻe fai ʻe ia foki; pea te ne fai mo ia ʻoku lahi hake; koeʻuhi ko ʻeku ʻalu ki heʻeku Tamai.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.
Pea ko e meʻa kotoa pē te mou kole ʻi hoku huafa, te u fai ia, koeʻuhi ke fakaongoongolelei ʻae Tamai ʻi he ʻAlo.
And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
Ko ia kotoa pē te mou kole ʻi hoku huafa, te u fai.
If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it.
“Kapau ʻoku mou ʻofa kiate au, fai ʻeku ngaahi fekau.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
Pea te u kole ki he Tamai, pea te ne foaki kiate kimoutolu ha Fakafiemālie ʻe taha, koeʻuhi ke nofo ia mo kimoutolu ʻo taʻengata;
And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever;
‌ʻIo, ko e Laumālie ʻoe moʻoni; ʻaia ʻoku ʻikai faʻa maʻu ʻe he māmani, he ʻoku ʻikai mamata ia ki ai, pe ʻiloʻi ia: ka te mou ʻilo ia; he te ne nofo mo kimoutolu, pea nofoʻia ʻe ia ʻakimoutolu.
Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
“ʻE ʻikai te u tuku ke tuēnoa ʻakimoutolu: te u haʻu kiate kimoutolu.
I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
‌ʻOku toe siʻi, pea ʻe ʻikai mamata kiate au ʻa māmani; ka te mou mamata kiate au: koeʻuhi ʻoku ou moʻui, ʻe moʻui ʻakimoutolu foki.
Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also.
‌ʻI he ʻaho ko ia te mou ʻilo ʻoku ou ʻi heʻeku Tamai, mo kimoutolu ʻiate au, mo au ʻiate kimoutolu.
At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.

“Ko ia ʻoku ne maʻu ʻeku ngaahi fekau, ʻo fai ki ai, ko ia ia ʻoku ʻofa kiate au: pea ko ia ʻoku ʻofa kiate au, ʻe ʻofa ʻa ʻeku Tamai kiate ia, pea te u ʻofa mo au kiate ia, pea te u fakahā au kiate ia.”
He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.
Pea lea ʻa Siutasi kiate ia, naʻe ʻikai ko ʻIsikaliote, “ʻEiki, ko e hā te ke fakahā ai koe kiate kimautolu, kae ʻikai ki māmani?”
Judas saith unto him, not Iscariot, Lord, how is it that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world?
Pea leaange ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Kapau ʻoku ʻofa ha tangata kiate au, te ne fai ʻeku lea: pea ʻe ʻofa ʻa ʻeku Tamai kiate ia, pea te mā omi kiate ia, ʻo nofomaʻu mo ia.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.
Ko ia ʻoku ʻikai ʻofa kiate au, ʻoku ʻikai te ne maʻu ʻeku ngaahi tala: pea ko e lea ʻoku mou ongoʻi, ʻoku ʻikai ʻaʻaku, ka ʻoku ʻae Tamai kuo ne fekauʻi au.
He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s which sent me.
“Ko e ngaahi meʻa ni kuo u tala kiate kimoutolu, ʻi heʻeku ʻiate kimoutolu.
These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you.

Ka ko e Fakafiemālie ko e Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni, ʻaia ʻe fekau ʻe he Tamai ʻi hoku huafa, te ne akoʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻi he meʻa kotoa pē, mo fakamanatuʻi ʻakimoutolu ʻi he meʻa kotoa pē, ʻaia kuo u leaʻaki kiate kimoutolu.
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.

“ʻOku ou tuku ʻae melino kiate kimoutolu, ko ʻeku melino ʻoku ou foaki kiate kimoutolu: ʻoku ʻikai hangē ko e foaki ʻa māmani, ʻa ʻeku foaki kiate kimoutolu. ʻOua naʻa mamahi homou loto, pea ʻoua naʻa manavahē ʻia.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

Kuo mou ongoʻi ʻeku lea kiate kimoutolu, ‘ʻOku ou ʻalu, pea u toe haʻu kiate kimoutolu.’ Ka ne mou ʻofa kiate au, te mou fiefia, ko e meʻa ʻi heʻeku pehē, ʻOku ou ʻalu ki he Tamai: he ʻoku lahi ʻeku Tamai ʻiate au.
Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I.
Pea ko eni kuo u fakahā ia kiate kimoutolu, ka ʻoku teʻeki hoko, koeʻuhi ʻoka hoko ia, ke mou tui.
And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe.
Ngata mei heni, ʻe ʻikai te u lea lahi kiate kimoutolu: he ʻoku haʻu ʻae ʻeiki ʻoe māmani, ka ʻoku ʻikai ha meʻa ʻiate au.
Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the prince of this world cometh, and hath nothing in me.
Ka koeʻuhi ke ʻilo ʻe māmani ʻoku ou ʻofa ki he Tamai; pea mo ʻeku fai ʻo hangē ko e fekau ʻae Tamai kiate au. “Tuʻu hake, ke tau ʻalu ʻi heni.
But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.
“Ko au ko e vaine moʻoni, pea ko ʻeku Tamai ko e tauhi ngoue ia.
I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
Ko e vaʻa kotoa pē ʻiate au ʻoku ʻikai fua, ʻoku ne tutuʻu ia: pea ko ia kotoa pē ʻoku fua, ʻoku ne ʻauhani ia, ke ʻāsili ai hono fua.
Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
Kuo mou maʻa eni, ʻi he lea kuo u lea kiate kimoutolu.
Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.
Nofo ʻiate au, mo au ʻiate kimoutolu. Hangē ʻoku ʻikai faʻa fua ʻae vaʻa ʻiate ia pē, ʻo kapau ʻe ʻikai nofo ʻi he vaine; pea ʻe pehē foki ʻakimoutolu, ʻo kapau ʻe ʻikai te mou nofo ʻiate au.
Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
“Ko au ko e vaine, ko e ngaahi vaʻa ʻakimoutolu: ko ia ʻoku nofo ʻiate au, mo au ʻiate ia, ko ia ia ʻe fua lahi: ka māvae mo au, ʻe ʻikai te mou faʻa fai ha meʻa.
I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
Kapau ʻe ʻikai nofo ha tangata ʻiate au, ʻoku liʻaki ia ʻo hangē ko e vaʻa ʻoku mate; pea tānaki ia ʻe he kakai, ʻo lī ki he afi, pea vela ai ia.
If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
Kapau ʻoku mou nofo ʻiate au, pea nofo ʻeku ngaahi lea ʻiate kimoutolu, te mou kole ʻaia te mou loto ki ai, pea ʻe fai ia kiate kimoutolu.
If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.
‌ʻI he meʻa ni ʻe ongoongolelei ai ʻa ʻeku Tamai, koeʻuhi ke mou fua lahi; ko ia te mou hoko ai ko ʻeku kau ākonga.
Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
Hangē ko e ʻofa ʻae Tamai kiate au, kuo pehē ʻeku ʻofa kiate kimoutolu: mou nofomaʻu ʻi heʻeku ʻofa.
As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.
Kapau ʻoku mou fai ʻeku ngaahi fekau, te mou nofo ʻi heʻeku ʻofa; ʻo hangē ko ʻeku fai ʻae ngaahi fekau ʻa ʻeku Tamai, pea u nofo ʻi heʻene ʻofa.
If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.
“Kuo u lea ʻaki ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kiate kimoutolu, koeʻuhi ke u maʻu maʻuaipē ʻae fiefia ʻiate kimoutolu, pea ke kakato ai hoʻomou fiefia.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
Ko ʻeku fekau eni, Ke mou feʻofaʻaki kiate kimoutolu, ʻo hangē ko ʻeku ʻofa kiate kimoutolu.
This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you.
‌ʻOku ʻikai ha tangata ʻe lahi hake ʻene ʻofa ʻi he meʻa ni, ke ne foaki ʻene moʻui koeʻuhi ko hono kāinga.
Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Ko hoku kāinga ʻakimoutolu, ʻo kapau ʻoku mou fai kotoa pē ʻaia ʻoku ou fekau kiate kimoutolu.
Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.

‌ʻOku ngata mei heni, ʻoku ʻikai te u ui ʻakimoutolu ko e kau tamaioʻeiki; he ʻoku ʻikai ʻilo ʻe he tamaioʻeiki ʻaia ʻoku fai ʻe hono ʻeiki: ka kuo u ui ʻakimoutolu ko e kāinga; he ko e meʻa kotoa pē kuo u fanongo mei heʻeku Tamai, kuo u fakaʻilo ia kiate kimoutolu.
Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.

Naʻe ʻikai te mou fili au, ka kuo u fili ʻakimoutolu, ʻo tuʻutuʻuni ʻakimoutolu, ke mou ʻalu atu, ʻo maʻu ʻae fua, pea ke tolonga homou fua: koeʻuhi ko ia kotoa pē te mou kole ki he Tamai ʻi hoku huafa, ke ne foaki kiate kimoutolu.

Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
Ko e meʻa ni ʻoku ou fekau kiate kimoutolu, ke mou feʻofaʻaki kiate kimoutolu.
These things I command you, that ye love one another.
“Kapau ʻoku fehiʻa ʻa māmani kiate kimoutolu, ʻoku mou ʻilo naʻe tomuʻa fehiʻa ia kiate au ʻiate kimoutolu.
If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
Ka ne ʻo māmani ʻakimoutolu, ʻe ʻofa ʻa māmani ki he meʻa ʻaʻana: ka koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ʻo māmani ʻakimoutolu, ka kuo u fili ʻakimoutolu mei māmani, ko ia ʻoku fehiʻa ai ʻa māmani kiate kimoutolu.
If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
Manatu ki he lahi ʻae tamaioʻeiki ki heʻene ʻeiki.’ Kapau kuo nau fakatangaʻi au, te nau fakatangaʻi ʻakimoutolu foki; kapau kuo nau fai ʻeku lea, te nau fai ʻa e lea ʻamoutolu foki.
Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
Ka te nau fai eni kotoa pē kiate kimoutolu koeʻuhi ko hoku huafa, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai te nau ʻilo ʻaia naʻa ne fekauʻi au.
But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me.
Ka ne ʻikai te u haʻu, ʻo lea kiate kinautolu, pehē, kuo ʻikai haʻanau angahala: ka ko eni, ʻoku ʻikai hano kofu ki heʻenau angahala.
If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin.
Ko ia ʻoku fehiʻa kiate au, ʻoku fehiʻa ki heʻeku Tamai foki.
He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
Ka ne ʻikai te u fai ʻae ngaahi ngāue ʻiate kinautolu naʻe ʻikai fai ʻe ha tokotaha, pehē, kuo ʻikai haʻanau angahala: ka ko eni, kuo nau mamata mo fehiʻa kiate au mo ʻeku Tamai.
If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
Ka ʻoku nau fakamoʻoni ʻae lea kuo tohi ʻi heʻenau fono, ‘Naʻa nau fehiʻa noa pē kiate au.’
But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
“Ka ʻoka haʻu ʻae Fakafiemālie, ʻaia te u fekau kiate kimoutolu mei he Tamai, ko e Laumālie ʻoe moʻoni, ʻoku ʻalu atu mei he Tamai, te ne fakamoʻoniʻi au:
But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
Pea ʻe fakamoʻoni mo kimoutolu foki, koeʻuhi naʻa mou ʻiate au talu mei he kamataʻanga.
And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
“Kuo u tala ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kiate kimoutolu, koeʻuhi ke ʻoua naʻa mou tūkia.
These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended.
Te nau kapusi ʻakimoutolu mei he falelotu: ʻio, ʻe hokosia ʻae kuonga, ko ia te ne tāmateʻi ʻakimoutolu, ʻe mahalo ʻe ia ko ʻene ngāue lelei ki he ʻOtua.
They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
Pea te nau fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni kiate kimoutolu, koeʻuhi naʻe ʻikai te nau ʻilo ʻae Tamai, pe ko au.
